## Part B: the debt band

The band uses the **debt service ratio** (monthly debt payments ÷ net monthly income): Green below 30%, Yellow 30% to below 60%, Red 60% or more (Bank Negara treats above 60% as vulnerable). Once Red, it stays Red until the ratio is below 55%; a better band shows only after 2 months in a row; no band is shown when typical income is below RM300.

- B1. These thresholds are reasonable for young Malaysian borrowers: ☐1 ☐2 ☐3 ☐4 ☐5
- B2. The debt service ratio is the right headline measure for this age group: ☐1 ☐2 ☐3 ☐4 ☐5
- B3. Waiting 2 months before showing a better band is sensible: ☐1 ☐2 ☐3 ☐4 ☐5
- Comment: ________

## Part D: the forecast and its reasons

Example as a user sees it: *"About 68 out of 100 people like you get into money trouble (a worse band or running short) in the next 3 months. What raises your risk: You ran short of money recently; Your cash cushion is smaller than average; Your typical monthly income is lower than average."* For someone already in Red, a line adds: *"You're already in Red, so this is the chance of running short of money."*

- D1. A young adult would understand what this means: ☐1 ☐2 ☐3 ☐4 ☐5
- D2. Showing a chance ("out of 100 people") rather than a yes/no warning is the right choice: ☐1 ☐2 ☐3 ☐4 ☐5
- D3. The reasons are things a person could act on: ☐1 ☐2 ☐3 ☐4 ☐5
